subject: Geography
description: Major Himalayan glaciers — Gangotri, Yamunotri, Siachen, Zemu, Pindari, Milam — sources of major rivers; climate change impact on Himalayan cryosphere.

questions.stem: GANGOTRI Glacier is the SOURCE of which major river?

options.option_text: Bhagirathi (origin of the Ganges)
Yamuna originates at Yamunotri
Brahmaputra (Tibet origin only)
Sutlej (Tibetan origin again)

questions.explanation: GANGOTRI GLACIER — one of the LARGEST glaciers in the Indian Himalaya (~30 km long, ~2-4 km wide, area ~143 sq km). Located in UTTARKASHI district of UTTARAKHAND, at altitude 4,000-7,000 m. SOURCE OF: BHAGIRATHI river — which joins the ALAKNANDA at DEVPRAYAG to form the GANGES (Ganga). The snout of Gangotri Glacier is called GAUMUKH ('cow's mouth' — the glacier's icy mouth resembles a cow). PILGRIMAGE: Gomukh is sacred — annual yatra. RETREAT: Gangotri has been retreating ~22 m/year on average over recent decades — mostly due to climate change. MAJOR RIVERS and their HIMALAYAN GLACIER ORIGINS: (1) BHAGIRATHI/GANGA → Gangotri Glacier. (2) ALAKNANDA → Satopanth + Bhagirath Kharak Glaciers (Garhwal). (3) YAMUNA → Yamunotri Glacier (also called Champasar Glacier). (4) MANDAKINI → Chorabari Glacier (Kedarnath). (5) GANDAK → Nepalese Himalayan glaciers. (6) KOSI → Khumbu region glaciers (Nepal). (7) BRAHMAPUTRA → Chemayungdung Glacier (Tibet, near Kailash). (8) INDUS → Sengge Khabab Glacier (near Kailash, Tibet). (9) SUTLEJ → Lake Rakshastal/Mansarovar (Tibet). PYQ FREQUENCY: river-glacier pairings appear in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: SIACHEN GLACIER, the world's highest battlefield, is located in:

options.option_text: Eastern Karakoram (Ladakh)
Western Himalayas of HP only
Central Nepal Himalayas now
Eastern Himalayas of Sikkim

questions.explanation: SIACHEN GLACIER — located in the EASTERN KARAKORAM range (NOT Himalaya proper) in LADAKH, India. Length ~76 km — the LONGEST glacier in the NON-POLAR REGIONS. Altitude 5,400-6,000 m at the snout; surrounding peaks 7,000+ m. NAME: 'Siachen' = 'place of the wild rose' in Balti language. STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE: WORLD'S HIGHEST BATTLEFIELD — Indian Army deployment since OPERATION MEGHDOOT (April 1984), under General K. Sundarji's plan. India holds the entire glacier and the SALTORO RIDGE west of it; Pakistan holds positions on the lower western slopes. CONFLICT: Siachen War — over 1000 deaths each side, mostly from WEATHER (frostbite, avalanches, altitude sickness — NOT combat). LIFE AT POSTS: temperatures down to −60°C; soldiers serve 90-day rotations. INDUS DRAINAGE: Siachen feeds the NUBRA RIVER → SHYOK RIVER → INDUS. STRATEGIC: dominates routes from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir to Aksai Chin (China). RECENT: 2016 avalanche killed 10 Indian soldiers at Sonam post — Lance Naik HANUMANTHAPPA was found alive after 6 days, died in hospital. ENVIRONMENTAL: glacier retreating ~5-8 m/year; concerns over military pollution. PYQ FREQUENCY: Siachen geography in UPSC, SSC, defence exams.

questions.stem: Which glacier is the source of the YAMUNA river?

options.option_text: Yamunotri Glacier (Champasar)
Gangotri Glacier feeds Ganga
Pindari Glacier of Kumaon area
Zemu Glacier of Sikkim alone

questions.explanation: YAMUNOTRI GLACIER — also known as CHAMPASAR GLACIER — source of the YAMUNA river. Located in UTTARKASHI district, UTTARAKHAND, at ~6,387 m altitude on the slopes of BANDARPUNCH peak. The actual source point is a SACRED hot spring at YAMUNOTRI temple (3,293 m altitude); the temple is one of the CHAR DHAM sites (along with Gangotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath). YAMUNA river: longest tributary of the Ganga (1,376 km). Joins Ganga at TRIVENI SANGAM, ALLAHABAD (Prayagraj) — the holy confluence. KEY YAMUNA TRIBUTARIES: Tons (largest), Hindon, Chambal, Betwa, Ken, Sind. KUMBH MELA: Allahabad's Maha Kumbh (every 12 years; Ardh Kumbh every 6) draws ~10+ crore pilgrims — one of the largest peaceful gatherings in human history. POLLUTION: Yamuna heavily polluted in Delhi stretch — efforts under National River Conservation Plan, Yamuna Action Plan. CHAR DHAM YATRA glaciers all-in-Garhwal: Yamunotri (Yamuna), Gangotri (Bhagirathi-Ganga), Kedarnath (Mandakini, Chorabari Glacier), Badrinath (Alaknanda, Satopanth Glacier). PYQ FREQUENCY: Char Dham + glacier links are top SSC, UPSC, NCERT geography MCQs.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: ZEMU Glacier, the largest glacier of the eastern Himalaya, lies in which Indian state?

options.option_text: Sikkim (eastern Himalayas state)
Arunachal Pradesh easternmost state
Uttarakhand of central Himalaya
Himachal Pradesh western Himalayas

questions.explanation: ZEMU GLACIER — largest glacier in the EASTERN HIMALAYAS, located in NORTH SIKKIM, on the eastern flank of KANGCHENJUNGA (the world's THIRD HIGHEST mountain at 8,586 m). Length: ~26 km. Altitude: ~4,000-7,000 m. SOURCE of the TEESTA RIVER (via the Zemu Chhu, which feeds the Lachen Chhu, then Teesta). KANGCHENJUNGA — five peaks (Sanskrit Kanchanjangha = 'five treasures of snow'); shared by Sikkim (India) and Nepal. First climbed: 1955 (British expedition led by Charles Evans; out of respect for Sikkimese beliefs, climbers stopped a few feet below summit — tradition continues). TEESTA RIVER: flows south through Sikkim and West Bengal; joins BRAHMAPUTRA in Bangladesh. Major hydropower potential — multiple ongoing projects. RECENT — OCT 2023: TEESTA-3 dam burst from a GLACIAL LAKE OUTBURST FLOOD (GLOF) — South Lhonak Lake glacier-lake breach killed 100+ in flash floods. Major reminder of climate-change risks. OTHER EASTERN HIMALAYA GLACIERS: Kanchenjunga's other glaciers (Talung, Yalung), Bhutanese glaciers (drain into Brahmaputra). PYQ FREQUENCY: state-glacier pairings in NCERT-driven SSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: PINDARI Glacier, a popular trekking destination, is located in:

options.option_text: Kumaon Himalaya (Uttarakhand)
Garhwal Himalaya (Uttarakhand)
Spiti Valley region (Himachal)
Kashmir Valley (Jammu region)

questions.explanation: PINDARI GLACIER — located in the KUMAON HIMALAYA, BAGESHWAR district of UTTARAKHAND. ~3 km long, altitude 3,353 m at zero-point (the trek's endpoint). Source of PINDAR RIVER, which flows into the ALAKNANDA at KARNAPRAYAG. POPULAR TREK: 'Pindari Glacier Trek' — gentle, moderate; reachable in ~5-6 days from base at Bharari/Loharkhet. Since 2013 floods, accessibility has been disrupted in places. KUMAON vs GARHWAL: both regions in Uttarakhand. KUMAON = eastern half (Almora, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Nainital, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar). GARHWAL = western half (Chamoli, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri, Rudraprayag, Uttarkashi, Dehradun, Haridwar). NEAR PINDARI: KAFNI Glacier (close trek), MILAM Glacier (longer, NEAR INDO-NEPAL-TIBET TRIJUNCTION) — Milam is the largest Kumaon glacier (~16 km long). NANDA DEVI (7,816 m): India's 2nd highest peak, in Chamoli; surrounded by Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve (UNESCO Heritage). NOTABLE TREKS in UTTARAKHAND: Valley of Flowers (Bhyundar), Kedarkantha, Roopkund (skeleton lake), Hemkund Sahib. PYQ ANGLE: Kumaon-Garhwal distinctions and glacier-trek locations in SSC, NDA, state PSC.

questions.stem: Which scientific organisation studies Himalayan glaciers and the cryosphere in India?

options.option_text: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology
Geological Survey of India primarily
National Atlas (NATMO) for maps
Indian Council of Agricultural Research

questions.explanation: WADIA INSTITUTE OF HIMALAYAN GEOLOGY (WIHG) — autonomous research institute under the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India. Established 1968 in DEHRADUN, Uttarakhand. Named after D.N. WADIA, a pioneer Indian geologist. PRIMARY FOCUS: geological studies of the Himalayan and adjoining regions — glaciology, seismology, tectonics, hydrology, paleobiology. KEY OUTPUTS: glacial mass-balance studies, retreat-rate measurements (e.g., Gangotri Glacier monitoring since 1990s). Documented that ~75% of Himalayan glaciers are RETREATING. RELATED ORGANIZATIONS: (1) NATIONAL CENTRE FOR POLAR AND OCEAN RESEARCH (NCPOR), Goa — runs Himadri (Arctic), Bharati & Maitri (Antarctic) stations; cryosphere research. (2) GEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA (GSI), Kolkata — broader geological mapping. (3) NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT (NIDM) — risks from glaciers (GLOFs, avalanches). (4) ICIMOD (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development), Kathmandu — Hindu Kush Himalaya Monitoring & Assessment Programme (HIMAP). CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACT: 2019 ICIMOD report — Himalayas could lose 1/3 of glaciers by 2100 even if 1.5°C warming target met. PYQ ANGLE: research-organization MCQs in UPSC PT, SSC GA.

questions.stem: A GLACIAL LAKE OUTBURST FLOOD (GLOF) is a sudden release of water from:

options.option_text: A glacier-fed lake breaching its dam
A river dam reservoir gates opening
Underground aquifer breaks the surface
Heavy monsoon rains in the basin

questions.explanation: GLOF = GLACIAL LAKE OUTBURST FLOOD — a sudden, catastrophic release of water from a glacier-dammed or moraine-dammed lake when its natural barrier breaks. CAUSE: glacial retreat creates LAKES at the snout (or in moraines) — held back by ice/loose-rock dams; breach is triggered by avalanche, earthquake, or simply gradual erosion. INDIAN HIMALAYA — recent MAJOR GLOFs: (1) UTTARAKHAND FLOODS, JUNE 2013 — Kedarnath disaster — 5,000+ deaths; Chorabari Lake outburst combined with cloudburst. (2) CHAMOLI, FEB 2021 — Rishi Ganga + Dhauliganga flash flood; killed 200+; ice-rock avalanche from a hanging glacier. (3) SIKKIM, OCT 2023 — South Lhonak Lake GLOF — killed 100+, destroyed Teesta-3 hydropower dam, displaced 25,000+. RISK ASSESSMENT: ~7,500+ glacial lakes in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region; ~25-30 are 'high-risk' GLOF candidates. WARNING SYSTEMS: India deploys SATELLITE MONITORING (ISRO), early-warning sensors at vulnerable lakes; ICIMOD does regional coordination. CLIMATE CHANGE LINK: warmer temperatures → faster glacier melt → larger and more numerous lakes → higher GLOF risk. PYQ ANGLE: GLOFs are rising in importance — UPSC PT/Mains/Geography optional 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests climate-disaster knowledge.

questions.stem: The Milam Glacier, one of the largest glaciers in the Kumaon Himalayas, is the primary source of which river?

options.option_text: Kali river, also known as the Sharda river system
Gori Ganga river, flowing through the Munsiyari valley
West Ramganga river in the Uttarakhand hill region
Saryu river, originating near the Sarju watershed area

questions.explanation: The Milam Glacier in Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand, is the principal source of the Gori Ganga river, which drains the Johar valley and meets the Kali river at Jauljibi. The Kali (Sharda) itself originates from the Kalapani-Lipulekh area, making Option A a plausible but incorrect distractor.

questions.stem: Which glacier, approximately 25 km in length, is the longest glacier entirely within Himachal Pradesh?

options.option_text: Bara Shigri Glacier in the Lahaul-Spiti district
Kulti Glacier situated in the Kullu river valley
Miyar Glacier located in the Chenab river catchment
Gepang Gath Glacier in the upper Spiti river zone

questions.explanation: Bara Shigri (also spelt Bada Shigri) in Lahaul-Spiti district stretches about 25 km, making it the longest glacier in Himachal Pradesh. The Miyar Glacier (Lahaul) is another significant glacier but is considerably shorter. Kulti and Gepang Gath are smaller glaciers in their respective sub-ranges.

questions.stem: The catastrophic 2013 Kedarnath disaster was significantly worsened by the sudden outburst of which glacial lake?

options.option_text: Satopanth Lake near the Badrinath pilgrimage site
Chorabari Lake, formed from the retreating Chorabari Glacier
Hemkund Lake in the Valley of Flowers national park
Vasuki Tal situated near the Mandakini river source

questions.explanation: Chorabari Lake (also called Gandhi Sarovar), a proglacial lake formed by the retreat of the Chorabari Glacier above Kedarnath, breached during the June 2013 cloudbursts, unleashing a devastating torrent of water, ice, and debris. Satopanth Lake (near Badrinath) and Hemkund Lake are unrelated to this event; Vasuki Tal lies near Gangotri, far from Kedarnath.

questions.stem: In glaciology, the 'Equilibrium Line Altitude' (ELA) on a Himalayan glacier marks the zone where:

options.option_text: The glacier terminus meets the outermost terminal moraine
Annual snow accumulation exactly equals annual ice ablation
Crevasses and seracs form due to differential ice flow speeds
Subglacial meltwater channels emerge at the glacier surface

questions.explanation: The ELA is the altitude on a glacier where net annual mass balance is zero — accumulation above equals ablation below. As climate warms, the ELA rises, progressively shrinking the accumulation zone. Option A conflates ELA with the glacier terminus; Option C describes icefalls and seracs caused by velocity differentials, an entirely separate phenomenon.

questions.stem: The Alaknanda river, a major headstream of the Ganga, originates from meltwater of which two glaciers near Mana village in Uttarakhand?

options.option_text: Gangotri Glacier and Milam Glacier at the Devprayag area
Satopanth Glacier and Bhagirath Kharak Glacier near Mana
Khatling Glacier and Kedarnath Glacier near Rudraprayag
Kedarnath Glacier and Pindari Glacier in the Chamoli area

questions.explanation: The Alaknanda rises from the confluence of meltwater from Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers near Mana village (the last Indian village before the China border), Chamoli district. This is distinct from the Bhagirathi, which rises at Gaumukh (Gangotri Glacier). Khatling Glacier feeds the Bhilangana, a Bhagirathi tributary — not the Alaknanda.

questions.stem: A Himalayan glacier that temporarily increases its flow velocity by 10 to 100 times over a period of months to years is said to be undergoing which process?

options.option_text: Jökulhlaup — a catastrophic subglacial flood outbreak
Glacier surge — brief dramatic speedup in ice flow velocity
Ablation cascade — rapid sequential surface ice melt event
Regelation creep — pressure melting and refreezing past obstacles

questions.explanation: A glacier surge is a short-lived episode of dramatically accelerated flow driven by instability in basal thermal or hydrological conditions. Jökulhlaup (Option A) is an outburst flood from a subglacial or proglacial lake — a wholly different phenomenon. Regelation (Option D) is a slow normal process of pressure-melting and refreezing around bedrock obstacles. 'Ablation cascade' is not a recognised glaciological term.

questions.stem: On a debris-covered Himalayan glacier, a 'supraglacial pond' typically forms when:

options.option_text: Meltwater pools on ice surface where the debris layer thins locally
Subglacial meltwater breaches through the glacier terminus rapidly
A lateral moraine collapse dams meltwater on the glacier margin
A jökulhlaup event drains a proglacial lake into the glacier body

questions.explanation: Supraglacial ponds develop where local thinning of the debris layer allows enhanced solar melting, creating depressions that fill with water directly on the ice surface; they accelerate mass loss through thermal erosion of surrounding ice walls. Option B describes subglacial drainage (not surface features); Option C produces ice-marginal or proglacial lakes, not supraglacial ponds; Option D is a GLOF event, the reverse of water entering a glacier.
